paragraphs: Jonathan ben Uzziel. He was the greatest of Hillel's approximately eighty students, as in Hyman’s citation to Sukkah 28b (compare [Sukkah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.28a.5-7)). And when he was engaged in Torah study, any bird that flew over him was immediately burned. (Hyman explains: The meaning is that any Torah scholar [supplied ת״ח] who opposed him in a matter of halakhah did not need extensive dialectic with him; with the mere breath of his mouth he showed him his error. I heard this from my friend, the dear rabbi R' Daniel HaKohen, מ״מ [unexpanded abbreviation; role uncertain] in the beit midrash [supplied בבה״מ] of Machzikei HaDat.)

In [Megillah 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.3a.4-5), Jonathan ben Uzziel transmitted the Targum of the Prophets on oral authority. Hyman explains מפי as “in the name of,” as in the testimony that R’ Yose transmitted from Shemaiah and Avtalyon (Hyman gives Yevamot 66a; compare [Yevamot 67a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.67a.12)). The Land of Israel [supplied א״י] quaked four hundred parasangs by four hundred parasangs; a heavenly voice [supplied ב״ק] went forth and said: Who is this who has revealed My secrets to human beings? Jonathan ben Uzziel [supplied ב״ע] stood on his feet and said: I am the one who revealed Your secrets. It is revealed and known before You that not for my own honor

nor for the honor of my father's house did I do it, but for Your honor, so that disputes would not multiply in Israel. (Hyman writes: Regarding the Targum Jonathan that we have today, whether it is from Jonathan ben Uzziel or whether it is later, the later sages have already discussed this at length, and this is not within the scope of our work.) And [Bava Batra 133b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.133b.12-13): there was an incident of a man whose sons did not behave properly; he arose and wrote his property over to Jonathan ben Uzziel [supplied ב״ע]. He sold a third and consecrated a third,

and returned a third to the man’s sons. Shammai came upon him with his staff and his knapsack. Jonathan said to him [the supplied א״ל does not name the speaker]: "Shammai, if you are able —" [the quotation is broken off as supplied]. Shammai said: Ben Uzziel has rebuffed me. Hyman concludes: From this we see his greatness, that Shammai, the Av Beit Din [supplied האב״ד], went to him.[^7]

notes.text: Abbreviation מ״מ is not in the empty acronym registry; left in Hebrew, role uncertain.

The seven whole saved Davidson Hebrew paragraphs and seven corresponding English paragraphs support the eighty-students and bird account at Sukkah 28a, the heavenly-voice dialogue at Megillah 3a, and Jonathan addressing Shammai in Bava Batra 133b–134a. Jonathan is made explicit as the contextual speaker of the supplied unnamed א״ל; rebuffed renders Shammai’s acknowledgment of the answer without implying angry railing. The supplied quotation still ends If you can—, without importing the rest of the Gemara’s argument. Hyman’s supplied Sukkah 28b citation, approximately eighty wording, Daniel HaKohen interpretation, unexpanded מ״מ office, מפי parenthesis and Targum-authorship question remain as supplied or attributed. The prophets named in the digital Megillah paragraph are not inserted into the supplied gap. All four current mixed notes remain verbatim, both source holds remain, and no printed-page correction history, Hillel-generation or Av Beit Din historical admission, authority binding, or extra primary figures and legal material is added.

Hyman’s printed notice (II, p. 702) gives Sukkah 28b. The consulted Davidson edition gives Hillel’s eighty students and the burning-bird account at 28a. Hyman says approximately eighty and credits R’ Daniel HaKohen for the explanation about a scholar’s error. The printed title next to Daniel’s name is מ״מ, whose expansion remains uncertain. In the explanation of מפי, the printed notice reads כמו משום where the supplied transcription reads כמו כשם. The cited testimony of R’ Yose from Shemaiah and Avtalyon is at Davidson Yevamot 67a, beside the printed 66a. Megillah 3a names Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi in the Prophets Targum passage. Hyman omits the names and separately leaves open who authored the Targum available in his time. Bava Batra 133b–134a confirms that Jonathan addresses Shammai and then Shammai acknowledges the rebuttal. Hyman’s printed quotation ends at “If you are able—”; the continuation belongs to the Talmud passage.

The linked Megillah names Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi as the authorities. Hyman’s abridgment leaves out those names and separately leaves the authorship of the extant Targum to other scholars. The dispute with Shammai continues at [Bava Batra 134a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.134a.1). [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1869&lang=en) collects the burning-bird account and the dispute as distinct episodes.
